records.claim: Fluoxetine gets into breastmilk, and most reports find no side effects in breastfed babies. In a small number of cases, irritability, vomiting, diarrhea, and less sleep have been reported. One study noted slightly less weight gain in infants exposed to fluoxetine via breast milk; however, this would likely only be an issue if the infant’s weight gain was already a concern. One study showed that mental and physical development was normal for infants exposed to fluoxetine in breastmilk in their first year of life. If you suspect the baby has any symptoms (such as irritability, vomiting, diarrhea, trouble sleeping, or trouble gaining weight) contact the child’s healthcare provider.
